scope: Fresh reread of the supplied F: groundwater-discharge packet, the March 13, 2025 N3862 violation notice and the second duplicate of the April 2, 2025 Wexford response. method: Computed SHA-256 and byte size for every locally available supplied source; matched hashes against all current catalogs before deciding whether to reuse or add a record.
Opened every locally available PDF, PDF-payload DOCX and PDF-payload HTML source and verified page counts. The F: packet contains 19 files and 111 pages; the March 13, 2025 notice contains 3 pages.

Rendered all 111 packet pages and all 3 notice pages in page order and inspected the visual sequence, maps, forms, signatures, tables, attachments and appendix pages. The existing eight-page VN response was already rendered and manually recovered in batch106; its second supplied copy was hash-checked as an exact duplicate.

Native text was coherent on 74 packet pages and all 3 notice pages. Thirty-seven packet pages are scan-only (the completed certification, six maps and the 30-page lagoon package). No bundled OCR engine was available in this environment; those pages were manually visually recovered from renders and claims are limited to what the source images support. OCR was not falsely claimed.

Preserved filename/content discrepancies: two files named .docx and one file named .html are valid PDF payloads; the construction-permit PDF and operating-license PDF share a base filename but are different records.

Applied the evidence boundary: permit capacity, public-notice steps, laboratory package, landfill authorization and air-compliance allegations are not treated as proof of a Cadillac WWTP receiving transaction, an exact final load date, PFAS concentrations in the WWTP, or a site-specific migration pathway.

verifiedFindings.finding: The Rule 2210(y) application and draft/final permit package proposes a one-time discharge of diluted landfill leachate from the evaporator lagoon, with a maximum of 50,400 gallons/day and 2,000,000 gallons/year, using overland flow and a spray bar. The final permit is effective October 1, 2016 and includes a six-month-or-less drawdown condition and a prohibition on adding new leachate to the lagoon during the authorized discharge.
verifiedFindings.boundary: These are application/authorization terms and capacity limits, not proof that the discharge occurred or that Cadillac received a particular load.

verifiedFindings.finding: The flow worksheet uses a 4.5-acre lagoon/spray-curtain footprint, a 35-gpm pump and approximately 900,000 gallons, with conservative precipitation assumptions; it estimates 30 April operating days or 38 May days depending on start timing.
verifiedFindings.boundary: The worksheet is a planning calculation, not a measured receiving-log or invoice record.

verifiedFindings.finding: DEQ's July 12, 2016 correspondence transmitted the public-notice package and directed the applicant to publish by July 15. The completed certification visually records posting at the landfill entrance beginning July 15, 2016 and is signed by a facility engineer; the separate certification form is blank.
verifiedFindings.boundary: The certification establishes the reported posting method/date, not newspaper publication or actual discharge.

verifiedFindings.finding: The six Golder figures provide regional site orientation, registered-well and wetland locations, a facility plan, and north/south topographic context for the lagoon, spray curtain, hose and proposed overland area.
verifiedFindings.boundary: The maps do not supply measured water levels, hydraulic tests, a current flow contour or a demonstrated PFAS source-to-Plett pathway.

verifiedFindings.finding: The 30-page lagoon summary is a scan of chain-of-custody pages, December 2015 lagoon sample results, laboratory parameter tables and QA/QC material.
verifiedFindings.boundary: It does not itself document Cadillac WWTP receiving, billing, per-load gallons or an exact final delivery date; unreadable scan values were not guessed.

verifiedFindings.finding: Construction Permit 4127 identifies Wexford County Landfill, LLC, facility ID 470336, as a 196.40-acre municipal solid-waste and Type III industrial-waste landfill, issued August 20, 2012; Operating License 9758 is issued November 19, 2024 through November 19, 2029 and incorporates Permits 4100/4127 and later monitoring and engineering plans.
verifiedFindings.boundary: Landfill authorization and incorporated plans do not prove a Cadillac receiving transaction or a PFAS migration route.

verifiedFindings.finding: EGLE's March 13, 2025 N3862 Violation Notice alleges failures involving annual NMOC reporting, GCCS installation, Subparts WWW/XXX notifications and MI-ROP-N3862-2022 special conditions. It requests a written response by April 3, 2025 and flare-flowrate data for January 2020 through January 2025.
verifiedFindings.boundary: This is an air-compliance notice and does not establish PFAS concentrations, WWTP receipt or the outcome of the enforcement matter.

verifiedFindings.finding: The second supplied copy of Wexford's April 2, 2025 response is byte-identical to record 066. The full eight-page response and embedded signed 2017 inspection were already reviewed in batch106; no second record or event was created.
verifiedFindings.boundary: The operator's LandGEM/GCCS explanation remains attributed to Wexford and is not an EGLE final adjudication.
